newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal Telecom profit soars to record in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Portugal Telecom profit soars to record in 1996.

text.p: State-controlled Portugal Telecom, the largest company on the Portuguese bourse, reported on Wednesday that profits surged 51 percent in 1996 to a record 54.9 billion escudos ($320 million).
The results were at the top end of analysts' forecasts and the company's stock on the Lisbon bourse rose at the start to a record high 6,650 escudos per share.
The shares later eased back to 6,568 escudos on profit-taking but the price was still up slightly on the previous close.
"There is no doubt that the results are good particularly as there are no big extraordinary (profit) gains," said Pierre Boule of Lisbon brokers Fincor.
The company said that it would propose a gross dividend of 138 escudos per share, up from 91 escudos in 1995 when it declared a profit of 36.3 billion escudos.
Portugal Telecom, which is due to be further privatised later this year, said that total revenues had risen 11.3 percent last year to 477.8 billion escudos.
Operating costs and expenses rose 9.1 percent to 350.3 billion escudos.
The state's stake in Portugal Telecom has been progressively cut to 51 percent and the Socialist government plans to float a further 26 percent later this year.
